design: Train target months <= 2020, test 2021-01..2025-12, pooled logistic regression on 67 units (53 countries, 4 Brazil subsystems, 10 US states); horizons 1-12 months; baselines climatology (unit x calendar month) and persistence; 300-resample block bootstrap over test months. Useful lead time = largest H with AUC-PR above persistence (90% interval > 1) at every horizon 1..H.

families.A_storage: G-REALM altimetry levels of reservoirs matched to GPPD hydro plants within 0.5 deg, capacity-weighted z per unit
families.B_snow: MODIS MOD10CM snow-cover z per unit box (snow units only), plus melt-season interaction
families.C_seasonal: IOD, PDO, CFSv2 forecast precip / 2 m temperature anomaly for the target month, CFSv2 Nino3.4 forecast

notes: Persistence = training-period P(shortfall at t+h | shortfall at t), pooled over units; climatology = unit x calendar-month frequency.
No data-latency adjustment: month t is assumed known at the end of month t (generation, rain, altimetry, snow, indices).
NMME is one model (NCEP-CFSv2), initialised in the issue month; CFSv2 reaches 9.5 months, so horizons 10-12 have no NMME precip/temperature (null -> missing flag).
The official CPC/IRI ENSO probability archive is not machine-readable; the CFSv2 Nino3.4 forecast stands in for it.
SWOT lake data begin 2023-07 and have no overlap with the <= 2020 training period, so SWOT is not used.
Satellite storage is a level anomaly (not volume) and covers 1-78% of each country's hydro capacity; there is a TOPEX-to-Jason-2 gap ~2002-2008.
Sources ids 'modis_mod10cm', 'nmme_cfsv2', 'psl_dmi', 'ncei_pdo', 'eia_bulk' are not in meta.json yet; listed in external_sources_not_in_meta.
